Subject: Post-call: GDPR DPA & SCC selection — next steps

Hi Alice / Samir,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Scope: AcmeHealth will be a controller for patient data; Redwood will act as processor for inference requests and temporary KV cache. Confirmed: no long-term storage of PHI on Redwood.
- Compliance items you asked about: SOC 2 status, DPA template, SCC module choice, and your vendor security questionnaire.
- Action items we agreed on: 
  1) I will share our standard DPA + SCC options and a short guidance doc on controller/processor implications (attached).
  2) Samir to send your security questionnaire; we will complete and return within 3 business days.
  3) Legal (Bob) to confirm whether Acme prefers SCC Module 2 (Controller-Processor) or Module 3.
  4) Rishi will follow up on SOC 2 timeline and whether any SOC attestation evidence is needed for procurement.

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Request_20270418.pdf (your DPA request), SCC_Module_Comparison.xlsx (our recommended starting point).

Next meeting: Proposed check-in Wed 4/21 10am PT — open to a different time if that works better.

If I missed anything, call it out — otherwise I'll send the DPA and SCC comparison now.

Subject: SOC 2 evidence + DPA/SCC options (AcmeHealth)

Hi Alice / team — looping in Neha from our privacy/security team to help on the DPA/SCC questions. Quick answers and attachments below.

SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II (Security & Availability) — report period 2026-05-01 to 2027-04-30. We can provide (1) SOC 2 report under NDA or (2) a SOC bridge letter if you need interim coverage. If procurement requires the last 12 months of evidence, we can grant an on-demand access link to the report once an NDA is in place.

DPA & SCC guidance (see attached SCC_Module_Comparison.xlsx): 
- For the scenario discussed (Acme as controller, Redwood as processor, no long-term storage of PHI), we typically recommend SCC Module 2. Module 2 maps to controller-processor relationships and includes processor-specific clauses.
- If Acme needs any cross-border subprocessors beyond our standard EU data flows, we can toggle to Module 3, but that often introduces extra operational constraints.

Vendor security questionnaire: we received the file — thanks. We'll start filling it out today and expect to return a completed copy by EOD Tue 4/20.

Neha, can you confirm the retention/kv cache policy and whether 30-day log retention is configurable per-customer?

Next steps:
- Marissa: send standard DPA + redline guidance (Marissa: attaching draft DPA).
- Neha: confirm retention and controller/processor wording suggestions.
- Bob (Acme legal): please flag any mandatory clauses you require so we can add to the first redline.

Thanks — Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Bob Lee <bob.legal@acmehealth.com>, Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence + DPA/SCC options (AcmeHealth)

Hi all — thanks for the context. A few technical and legal alignment points from privacy/security: 

1) Retention & KV cache: Redwood's default KV cache for inference is ephemeral; we persist KV cache only for the duration of the request by default. We offer configurable short-term logging for debugging (configurable up to 30 days) which can be disabled. If Acme requires "no logs" beyond transient telemetry, we can disable customer-level logging for your account.

2) PHI / De-identification: De-identified patient summaries are acceptable under GDPR as long as they are truly irreversible. Operationally, our guidance is to hash / remove direct identifiers prior to sending. We recommend documenting the de-identification process in the DPA appendix.

3) SCC module suggestion: Given the controller (Acme) / processor (Redwood) structure you described and no planned use of our downstream subprocessors for storage, Module 2 is appropriate. We'll mark Module 2 as the default but can discuss Module 3 if Acme's legal asks for additional transfer safeguards.

4) DPA redline: I'll circulate a short privacy-focused redline calling out: data categories, retention window, subprocessors, and security controls. Marissa/Rishi: please take the first pass and I'll review.

Attachments: Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Filled.docx (completed responses), suggested_DPA_clauses.txt

If that aligns, Marissa — please send the DPA draft to Bob and we'll plan a redline call if needed.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
